moments.title: The war ends, the American century begins
moments.advantage: half of world industrial output, 80% of the gold
moments.mechanism: The only large economy not bombed produced half of global industrial output and held most of the gold, so it wrote the monetary rules and paid for Europe's recovery.
moments.outcome: Bretton Woods put the dollar at the centre; the Marshall Plan moved US$13.3 billion to 17 countries; US GDP was 1,474 billion 1990 dollars in 1945 against the USSR's 343, and 1,456 against 510 in 1950.

moments.title: The transistor at Bell Labs
moments.mechanism: Three Bell Labs physicists made the transistor at a laboratory that employed 9,000 by the war's end, part of the Bell System.
moments.outcome: Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley shared the 1956 Nobel Prize; Bell Labs work has since won eleven Nobel Prizes in all (a count to 2026).

moments.title: The traitorous eight
moments.mechanism: Eight engineers walked out of Shockley's laboratory of 32, found a backer in Sherman Fairchild, and bet on silicon when germanium was the norm.
moments.outcome: Fairchild was founded on 18 September 1957 with $1.38 million; its first marketed transistor, the 1958 2N697, sold in a first batch of 100 to IBM at $150; by 1960 its sales exceeded $20 million.

moments.title: The planar process and the monolithic integrated circuit
moments.mechanism: Fairchild developed the planar process in 1959 and Robert Noyce invented the monolithic integrated circuit; Kilby's 1958 circuit at Texas Instruments was a hybrid.
moments.outcome: Fairchild licensed Hoerni's planar 2N1613 across the industry.

moments.title: The microprocessor
moments.mechanism: Intel's silicon-gate process put 2,300 transistors on one chip, built for Busicom.
moments.outcome: Intel introduced the 4004 in 1971; in 1975 Moore revised his forecast to a doubling every two years.

moments.title: The IBM PC and the x86 lock-in
moments.advantage: the chip inside the IBM PC and its clones
moments.mechanism: The IBM PC used an Intel 8088; after Japanese memory makers squeezed Intel's profits in 1983, Andy Grove refocused it on microprocessors, and Compaq's 1986 80386 system beat IBM to the next chip and made Intel a key component supplier.
moments.outcome: Intel became a microprocessor company: the 4004's field became its primary business only in the early 1980s, while IBM's 1980 gross income was $26.2 billion and Compaq's sales reached $329 million in 1986.

moments.title: The pure-play foundry
moments.mechanism: A joint venture of Taiwan's government, ITRI and private investors, with Philips taking 27.6 percent for $58 million and the government's development fund providing 48.3 percent of the capital, became the world's first dedicated foundry.
moments.outcome: TSMC held 72.5% of top-10 foundry revenue in Q2 2026 and 79% of its Q3 2026 wafer revenue came from 7nm and below.

moments.title: The GeForce 256, the first GPU
moments.mechanism: After cutting its staff from 100 to 40 in 1996, Nvidia put 17 million transistors, made by TSMC, on the GeForce 256, its first product marketed as a GPU.
moments.outcome: Nvidia listed in January 1999 with $0.37 billion of revenue, level with 3dfx's $360.5 million that year; in December 2000 it agreed to acquire 3dfx's intellectual assets.

moments.title: CUDA opens the GPU to programmers
moments.advantage: a development environment for its chips
moments.mechanism: Created in 2004 and released in 2007, CUDA is Nvidia's development environment.
moments.outcome: CUDA was downloaded 150 thousand times in 2008 and counted more than 120,000 developers in 2011; in March 2026, twenty years old by Nvidia's count, it had 6 million developers.

moments.title: AlexNet on two GTX 580s
moments.advantage: deep learning trained on its GPUs
moments.mechanism: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton trained a 60-million-parameter network for five to six days on two GTX 580s, $500 each.
moments.outcome: Top-5 error 15.3%, more than 10.8 points ahead of the runner-up.

moments.title: Attention Is All You Need
moments.advantage: an architecture that parallelises on GPUs
moments.mechanism: Eight Google researchers built the Transformer on attention alone; earlier models with recurrence had been hard to accelerate on GPUs. The base model trained in 12 hours and the big model in 3.5 days on eight P100 GPUs, and Google published it.
moments.outcome: The big model had 213 million parameters; the paper has been cited more than 150,000 times; all eight authors later left Google.

moments.title: OpenAI scales the transformer
moments.advantage: the bet that loss falls as a power law with scale
moments.mechanism: Kaplan et al. showed loss falls as a power law in size, data and compute; OpenAI built GPT-3, ten times larger than any prior dense model and 3,640 petaflop/s-days of training, after Microsoft invested $1 billion in 2019.
moments.outcome: Parameters went 117 million (2018), 1.5 billion (2019), 175 billion (2020); Microsoft licensed GPT-3 exclusively in September 2020; OpenAI was valued at $14 billion in 2021 and $29 billion in 2023.

moments.title: ChatGPT
moments.advantage: distribution: a product anyone could use
moments.mechanism: A chat interface on a scaled transformer reached 100 million monthly users in two months, with Microsoft adding $10 billion and Azure compute in January 2023.
moments.outcome: 900 million weekly users by February 2026; OpenAI valued at $29 billion in 2023, $500 billion in October 2025 and later $852 billion.

moments.title: The AI revolution reaches Nvidia
moments.advantage: the largest share of AI accelerators
moments.mechanism: Nvidia went from $1 trillion to $2 trillion in 180 days and became the first company worth $5 trillion on 29 October 2025.
moments.outcome: Nvidia is valued at $4.506 trillion in November 2026; analysts project a 75% accelerator share for 2026, down from a peak near 87% in 2024.

moments.title: DeepSeek's cheaper model
moments.mechanism: DeepSeek-V3, by its authors' account, needed only 2.788 million H800 GPU hours to train.
moments.outcome: NVIDIA lost over $589 billion of market value in a day, then recovered and passed $5 trillion in October.

moments.title: The hyperscalers' capex wall
moments.mechanism: Five hyperscalers are forecast to spend $803 to $828 billion in 2026; Daloopa finds that over eight quarters NVIDIA's data-centre revenue equalled 39% to 47% of hyperscaler capex, 45% in the latest quarter it measured.
moments.outcome: NVIDIA's revenue was $96.2 billion in the quarter to 26 July 2026, with $279 billion of purchase commitments.

periods.what: Fairchild's alumni found dozens of firms, Intel among them.

periods.title: Foundry and fabless
periods.what: TSMC, the first dedicated foundry, makes chips designed by others, Nvidia's among them.

periods.title: Deep learning on GPUs
periods.what: AlexNet trains on two Nvidia GPUs; Nvidia's market value rises from $7.66 billion at the end of 2012 to $117.26 billion at the end of 2017.

periods.title: The scaling era
periods.what: The transformer is published; OpenAI scales it to GPT-3, with Microsoft's investment.

periods.title: The AI revolution
periods.what: ChatGPT, Nvidia's trillions, and valuations near a trillion dollars for two labs.

Second pass: Bell Labs' 1945 size is the wartime peak (no 1947 headcount was found); Intel's 1981 and 1987 revenue, TI's 1959 size, Fairchild's 1971 size, a 1987 size for Taiwan and TSMC's own first-year size were not found in script-readable sources; Krizhevsky's Wikidata birth year (2000) is implausible and is left empty; TSMC's foundry share around 1999 and 2012 and discrete-GPU share in 2007 were not found, so the moats of TSMC and NVIDIA are split by period and cite revenue, adoption and Jon Peddie's all-graphics share instead.
